name: Sterling-Nakamura Diplomatic Protection Cane DPC-1 'Ambassador'
description: An elegant walking cane concealing three weapon systems: a 50cm monocrystalline steel blade hidden within the shaft, a single-shot 10mm derringer built into the handle, and a contact taser in the ferrule capable of delivering a 100,000V discharge. Sterling-Nakamura issues the DPC-1 to senior diplomatic staff as a personal defense weapon that maintains the appearance of civilian propriety while providing lethal capability. The cane is constructed from carbon fiber with brass fittings and weighs slightly more than a standard walking cane — not enough to draw suspicion. The blade deploys with a twist-pull of the handle, the derringer fires with a concealed trigger in the grip, and the taser activates by pressing the ferrule firmly against a target.
specifications:
blade: 50 cm monocrystalline steel, concealed in shaft
derringer: Single-shot 10mm, handle-mounted, 5-meter range
taser: 100,000V contact discharge in ferrule
cane length: 95 cm
cane weight: 0.9 kg
construction: Carbon fiber shaft, brass fittings
blade deployment: Twist-pull handle, 0.5 seconds
derringer reload: Breech-load single round
story_hooks: A diplomat killed an assailant with a DPC-1 blade at a state function — the self-defense was legally justified, but the weapon's existence is now public knowledge and every diplomatic meeting has become a security concern.
Counterfeit DPC-1 canes are being manufactured with lower quality materials — the blades snap during use and the derringers misfire, turning a reliable weapon into a liability.
related_entities: Kessler Kinetics VelocityFrame MkIV Sprint Leg

physical_description.visual_profile: An elegant, refined walking cane with the bearing of refined diplomatic accessories—straight shaft tapering subtly toward a polished ferrule, topped with a slightly bulbous handle suggesting traditional craftsmanship rather than tactical purpose. The overall silhouette reads as civilian professional, deliberately understated.
physical_description.dimensions: 95 cm total length, shaft diameter 2.2 cm, handle circumference 8.5 cm, ferrule diameter 2.8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Noticeably denser than a standard cane despite its slender profile—balanced slightly forward toward the ferrule, giving it purposeful heft without obvious weaponization
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon fiber shaft with polished brass fittings and ferrule, hardwood grip inlay
physical_description.finish: Matte graphite carbon fiber shaft with mirror-polished brass accents; handle grip exhibits subtle wood grain under clear lacquer
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray carbon fiber with warm antique brass fittings; handle in rich walnut or ebony wood tone
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth hardwood with fine crosshatch texture underneath—professional, comfortable grip with no obvious tactical knurling; slight friction without aggression
distinctive_features: Concealed seam running the shaft length where blade retracts—barely visible unless examined closely
Subtle twist-grooves in the upper handle suggesting the deployment mechanism
Breech-load access point disguised as decorative brass collar beneath the handle
Ferrule with barely-perceptible contact points for the taser system
Sterling-Nakamura maker's mark engraved in elegant serif font on the brass band
Serial number etched discretely on the shaft near the base
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo (interlocking SN monogram) engraved on the brass band 12cm below handle; diplomatic authorization stamp on the ferrule collar
physical_description.condition_typical: Immaculate, polished, maintained like a luxury accessory—no battle wear, though may show light handling marks from diplomatic use; kept pristine by design
